A1.title: A coffee machine for a tea drinker

lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about shopping.
Sam, what is that big box?
It's a coffee machine! I bought it on Saturday.
Sam. You drink tea.
I know! But listen. I went to a shop, a big store. I looked around. A man came to me. I said, "Just looking, thanks."
And then?
Then I saw this box. I picked it up.
Was it expensive?
I asked, "How much is it?" The man said, "The price? Only forty manats!" So cheap! Not expensive.
Hmm. Cheap is not good for you. You do not drink coffee!
I had no cash, no money. So I asked, "Can I pay by card?"
And?
"Yes," he said. And he gave me a bag. A very big bag.
A big bag for a big mistake.
[laugh] Maybe. I put on my coat. I took the box. I went home. Leyla, do you want a coffee?
Yes, please!
Great. Can you show me how it works?
[laugh] Bye for now!

A2.title: A coffee machine for a tea drinker

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is shopping. And I have a story.
Is it about the coffee machine in your kitchen?
How do you know?! OK. On Saturday there was a big sale in town. There was a long queue outside the shop.
You waited in a queue? You hate queues.
I know! But the discount was big. Inside, I tried on a jacket. It was too small. "Do you have this in a bigger size?" I asked. No.
So you bought nothing?
Worse. I picked out a coffee machine. "It's on sale," said a customer next to me. "Buy it!"
Sam. You drink tea.
I know. I paid, and the cashier gave me back my card and the receipt. I put the receipt in my pocket. Then I lost it on the bus.
Oh no. Didn't you look online first?
I did. After I paid. The same machine was ten manats cheaper on the internet.
Sam! [laugh] So where is the machine now?
In my kitchen. Every morning it looks at me, like a sad dog.
Sell it to me! I love coffee. Here are fifty manats. Keep the change.
Fifty? I paid forty! So I made a profit. Maybe I'm a good shopper after all.
[laugh] Or maybe you're just lucky. See you next time!

B1.title: A coffee machine for a tea drinker

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is shopping — and yes, I have a confession.
[laugh] Is it about the coffee machine?
How does everyone know?! OK. Last Saturday, a sign in a shop window: fifty percent off coffee machines. What a bargain! Ten minutes later I was walking home with a brand new machine.
Sam. You drink tea. That's the perfect impulse buy.
I know. So on Monday I went to take it back. I wanted a refund.
And?
No receipt, no refund. The manager said, "I can only offer you an exchange."
Fine. Exchange it for something you actually use. A kettle!
That was my plan. But the normal kettles were out of stock. In fact, they had run out of everything except one.
Cheap kettles always sell out in winter. So what was left?
A gold kettle. Italian. A hundred and twenty manats.
That sounds like it costs an arm and a leg.
It does! I paid the difference — eighty manats.
Sam! You paid eighty manats for a kettle you didn't want an hour before?
I wanted it more in the shop. The light was very good.
I couldn't afford a kettle like that. Why didn't you shop around? There are five kettle shops on your street.
I know, I know. Next time I'll order online. Delivery is free after fifty manats.
Or buy second-hand. My neighbour sold me a lovely kettle for ten manats. It's not gold, but the tea is the same.
Now you tell me.
So how is the gold kettle?
Honestly? Best tea of my life. It boils in one minute, and it looks like a trophy.
Then it was worth every penny.
Don't tell the manager. He thinks he tricked me.
[laugh] Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is the best — or the worst — thing you have ever bought? Bye for now!
